text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages with eight quote variants each for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the Kalabo Hills School Meals Initiative volunteer team. Each morning you will help cooks at Sanwi Primary prepare hot porridge for roughly 340 pupils before the first bell at 7:30. Portions must weigh 250 grams, and you should check two bowls per class with the kitchen scale. Do not serve food that has been left uncovered for more than twenty minutes. In 2023, volunteers who followed the hygiene checklist helped cut reported stomach complaints by 40 percent. Remember that teachers, not volunteers, record attendance on the meal register. If a child refuses to eat, never force them; instead, note their name and inform the head cook at the end of service.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2024, field officers from the Tamarind Valley Savings Network visited 18 village savings and loan groups across Ondera district. Members had saved a combined 4.2 million shillings, an increase of 12 percent since the previous visit. Loan repayment remained strong, with 93 percent of loans repaid on schedule. However, two groups in Mbeleko had not held a share-out meeting since March, and their record books were incomplete. Officers did not find evidence of misused funds, but they recommended refresher training for treasurers. Women made up seven in ten group members, and most loans were used to buy seed or livestock.

passages.source_passage: As a hygiene volunteer with the Brightwater Rural Wells Trust, you will support households in Koro and Lendi villages after their new borehole opens in June 2025. Each volunteer is assigned about 25 households and should visit each one at least twice a month. During visits, demonstrate handwashing with soap for a full twenty seconds and check that the latrine cover is in place. Do not criticise families whose latrines are unfinished; offer to connect them with the local mason instead. Pump committee members, not volunteers, collect the monthly maintenance fee of 500 francs. Report any broken pump handle to the committee chair within 48 hours.

passages.source_passage: In 2024, the Lantern Evening Learning Network ran 42 literacy circles in market towns across the Seralo region, reaching 1,150 adult learners. Classes met three evenings a week, and 68 percent of enrolled learners completed the full nine-month cycle. Facilitators reported that many learners could now read medicine labels and bus timetables for the first time. Attendance dipped sharply during the harvest season, and we did not reach our target of 1,400 learners. Six circles closed because volunteer facilitators relocated, and no replacements were found before the year ended. With continued support from the fund, we plan to open eight new circles and introduce a numeracy module in 2025.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2025, the Safe Haven Case Management Unit in Dolwe camp opened 276 new protection cases, of which 41 percent involved unaccompanied or separated children. Caseworkers completed initial assessments within 72 hours for most cases, although the target of 90 percent was not met in April. Referrals to medical and legal partners rose steadily over the period. Eleven survivors of violence declined referral, and staff did not pressure them to change their decision. A shortage of female interpreters meant that some women waited up to two weeks for a follow-up interview. The unit has never shared case files with camp security without written consent.

passages.source_passage: Rainfall in the Kesura plateau has fallen by roughly 18 percent since 2000, and the last three planting seasons have each started late. Most of the 3,200 smallholder households in our target area still plant a single maize variety that does not tolerate long dry spells. In 2022, a pilot run by the Greenfield Dryland Collective introduced sorghum and cowpea seed to 150 farmers, and their average yields held steady despite a failed rainy season. Local seed traders do not currently stock drought-tolerant varieties, so farmers must travel over 60 kilometres to buy them. This proposal seeks to scale the pilot to six villages.

passages.source_passage: Board members will be pleased to hear that the Mvuli District Health Partnership now supports 210 community health workers across 14 sub-counties. Since last October, these workers have conducted more than 9,000 household visits and referred 612 children with danger signs to health centres. Stock-outs of oral rehydration salts remain a concern, and in February five sub-counties had no supplies for nearly three weeks. Monthly stipends were not paid on time in December because of a banking delay, which affected morale. The partnership's supervisors have since introduced a mobile payment system. We expect the county government to begin co-funding stipends in July 2026.

passages.source_passage: Volunteer mentors at the Harbourline Skills Centre work alongside instructors in the welding, tailoring and solar installation workshops. Each cohort has 30 trainees aged 18 to 25, and the course runs for 16 weeks. Your main role is to help trainees prepare CVs and practise job interviews during Friday afternoon sessions. Do not promise trainees a job placement; only the employer liaison officer can confirm apprenticeships. Last year, 74 percent of graduates found paid work within six months. Trainees who miss more than three sessions are not eligible for the final certificate, so please encourage regular attendance.

passages.source_passage: The Riverbend Malaria Free Campaign distributed 48,500 long-lasting insecticidal nets across Sutamo and Kwele districts between 3 and 21 March 2025. Household registration teams estimated that one net was needed for every two people, and 88 percent of registered households received their full allocation. District supervisors accompanied volunteer monitors on spot checks in 120 homes, which found that nets were hanging over sleeping spaces in most cases. However, some families had not removed the nets from their packaging, citing a strong chemical smell. Distribution in the island communities of Kwele was delayed by four days because the boat wasn't available. No stock was reported lost or stolen during transport.

passages.source_passage: Over the 2024 reporting year, the Nirmala Mothers' Outreach Project worked with four government clinics in the hill district of Pashani. Outreach nurses registered 2,340 pregnant women, and 79 percent of them attended at least four antenatal check-ups, up from 52 percent at baseline. Trained birth companions accompanied women to clinics for 1,105 deliveries. No maternal deaths were recorded among registered women during the year. However, the project did not meet its target for postnatal home visits within 48 hours of birth, largely because monsoon landslides blocked roads in July and August. We are grateful to the foundation for its flexible funding, which allowed us to hire two additional nurses.
